effect_estimate.comment: Both Table 4 rounded estimates (OR = 4.27, 95% CI: 3.07-5.93) and text 3-decimal estimates (OR = 4.269, 95% CI: 3.073-5.931) are reported verbatim in Chapter 4. Mean OWTS correction cost in Portage County was $13,700 (SD $6,946; range ~$560 to >$34,000; PDF p. 92).
effect_estimate.value: In descriptive analysis of 1,021 failed onsite wastewater treatment systems (OWTSs), 63.86% (311/487) of failures detected via Point-of-Sale (POS) property-transfer inspections achieved correction compliance within the 120-day Board of Health Notice of Violation (BOH NOV) deadline, compared to 19.85% (106/534) of non-POS failures (overall compliance: 40.84%, 417/1,021). In binary logistic regression (n = 938), POS inspection strongly increased the odds of timely compliance within 120 days in both the unadjusted model (OR = 7.225, 95% CI: 5.389-9.686, p < 0.0001) and the multivariable adjusted model (OR = 4.27 [text: 4.269], 95% CI: 3.07-5.93 [text: 3.073-5.931], p < 0.0001). In the adjusted model, connecting to a public sanitary sewer vs. traditional OWTS (OR = 0.33 [0.332], 95% CI: 0.14-0.81 [0.136-0.809], p = 0.02 [0.0153]), component repair vs. full replacement (OR = 0.32 [0.316], 95% CI: 0.18-0.56 [0.178-0.559], p = 0.0001 [< 0.0001]), higher correction cost per $1,000 (OR = 0.87 [0.866], 95% CI: 0.80-0.90 [0.803-0.904], p = 0.0001 [< 0.0001]), and older system age per 10 years (OR = 0.93 [0.925], 95% CI: 0.86-0.99 [0.864-0.991], p = 0.028 [0.0275]) significantly reduced odds of 120-day compliance, whereas alternative vs. traditional OWTS replacement was not statistically significant (OR = 1.75 [1.751], 95% CI: 0.90-3.39 [0.904-3.392], p = 0.10 [0.0965]).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by observational non-quasi-experimental study design. Assigned 2 because the study directly tracks administrative inspection, BOH Notice of Violation (NOV) enforcement, permitting/remediation pathway, and exact 120-day compliance completion records across 1,021 failed OWTS cases in Portage County Health District databases, while private real-estate escrow and household wealth sub-mechanisms are discussed inferentially rather than directly measured.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Observational administrative-record binary logistic regression without a quasi-experimental intervention identification strategy (POS inspection in Portage County is a voluntary property-transfer service rather than an assigned intervention) and without multi-wave longitudinal cohort structure; covariates include concurrent correction attributes (cost, repair vs. replacement, new system type), matching JBI Analytical Cross Sectional Studies appraisal (note: even if viewed as a retrospective administrative follow-up cohort over the 120-day NOV window, the CODEBOOK §9 certainty ceiling remains 2).

sample_size.comment: From 1,751 initial inspection records (Jan 2, 2015-June 30, 2023), 481 duplicates/incomplete/out-of-period records were removed leaving 1,270 inspected OWTSs; excluding 203 functioning systems left 1,067 failed OWTSs, of which 46 unclassified voluntary inspections were excluded, yielding 1,021 failed OWTS records for descriptive analysis and 938 complete cases for logistic regression (83 excluded for missing covariates).
